div.div: DML write sets, relationships, guards and retry behavior. Each TX is an implementation contract, not a stored procedure already installed.

div.div: TX-09 / Verified payment inbox, late success and duplicate charge

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 654px; height: 1px; padding-top: 218px; margin-left: 64px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.div:
GUARDS
Provider authentication verified before accepted inbox; expected target, amount, currency,
merchant and environment checked. Browser return URL is not evidence.
LOCK / CONSISTENCY
Persist inbox with unique provider event key; processing transaction locks event then
domain rows and marks inbox processed atomically.
DATABASE WRITES
INSERT provider_event; record authoritative attempt result. If fulfillment eligible run
TX-08. Else retain extra/late success and INSERT refund+outbox compensation. Reconciliation
queries provider outside transaction and feeds same handler.
RELATIONSHIP EFFECT
Do NOT add a unique successful payment per order: two external charges may truly succeed.
Only chosen fulfillment FK is unique; each charged attempt may have one logical refund.
FAILURE / RETRY
Repeated event with different payload hash is rejected. Out-of-order failure never demotes
succeeded payment. Wrong amount/currency never fulfills; escalate/reconcile/refund any
captured money safely.

div.div: TX-10 / Claim ticket and issue attendee entry confirmation

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 654px; height: 1px; padding-top: 218px; margin-left: 804px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.div:
GUARDS
Active verified claimant email matches order item recipient; ticket unclaimed or already
assigned to same account. Confirmation requires claimed valid ticket and current attendee
session.
LOCK / CONSISTENCY
Lock user/session then organization/event, ticket/claim/entry confirmation.
DATABASE WRITES
Consume claim token once; SET ticket recipient_user_id/claimed_at without changing order
buyer; INSERT short-lived entry_confirmation. Store only digest/key ID; publish no personal
info in QR.
RELATIONSHIP EFFECT
Composite confirmation FK requires attendee_user_id equal ticket.recipient_user_id; session
FK binds session to same user. Resending PDF preserves ticket identity.
FAILURE / RETRY
Wrong account/expired token rejected. A claimed ticket cannot be reassigned by ordinary
flow. Replaced claim is explicitly revoked before inserting new active claim.

div.div: TX-11 / Online check-in or manual admission

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 654px; height: 1px; padding-top: 717px; margin-left: 64px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.div:
GUARDS
Both attendee and scanner authenticated; device owned; current same-event scan permission;
event entrance gate open; token purpose correct; confirmation/session unexpired; ticket
valid.
LOCK / CONSISTENCY
Lock involved users/sessions and organization membership first; then event, ticket,
confirmation and check_in rows. Event lock serializes refunds and admission.
DATABASE WRITES
INSERT check_in; consume entry_confirmation; ticket valid -> checked_in; increment event
availability_version; INSERT audit/broadcast outbox in same commit.
RELATIONSHIP EFFECT
One unreversed check_in per ticket through partial unique index. Device+operation ID
unique. Entry confirmation may be consumed by only one check_in.
FAILURE / RETRY
Second scan sees already-used. Refund winning mutex makes scan fail; scan winning first
makes voluntary refund require reversal/review. A duplicate operation returns original
result, never a second admission.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 661px; margin-left: 806px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #FFFFFF;
display: inline-block; font-size: 17px; font-family: Arial; color: light-dark(#FFFFFF, #121212); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 654px; height: 1px; padding-top: 698px; margin-left: 804px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.div:
GUARDS
Explicit reverse_checkin permission; existing current accepted admission; reason required.
LOCK / CONSISTENCY
Lock auth/org/event then ticket/check_in.
DATABASE WRITES
INSERT check_in_reversal; set check_in.reversed_at to reversal timestamp; ticket checked_in
-> valid unless already invalidated by authorized event cancellation; audit and publish
count update.
RELATIONSHIP EFFECT
Original check_in stays; UNIQUE(check_in_id) allows one reversal. The old confirmation
stays consumed; next entry requires fresh confirmation/new check_in.
FAILURE / RETRY
Do not restore refunded/cancelled validity. Repeating reversal is idempotent. No deletion
of accepted check-in history.
